subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Writing an ending; good and bad restaurants; analysing essay structure / Planning and writing a narrative essay about an eating-out experience
outcomes: Know the parts of a narrative essay and their purpose
Plan and write a narrative essay about eating out

tf.s: 'Delicious food' and 'reasonable prices' describe a good restaurant.

tf.why: Attentive service means staff care for you, so it is good.
Right, nobody wants dirty knives and forks.

tf.s: The model essay has five paragraphs.
A topic sentence is usually the last sentence of a paragraph.
tf.why: It is usually the first sentence and gives the main idea.

tf.s: 'First, then, after that, finally' are linking words that show sequence.
tf.why: Yes, they show the order of events.

tf.s: When you write the story ending, you should copy sentences from the text.
tf.why: Use your own ideas for the ending.

tf.s: Sharing ideas with a group before writing helps you get ideas and feedback.
tf.why: Yes, others can help you improve your plan.

tf.s: A narrative essay does not need a title.
tf.why: Your essay needs a suitable title.

tf.s: 'Our waiter was efficient, helpful and friendly' is a supporting detail.
tf.why: Well done, it supports the main idea.

boxes.q: Which phrase describes a bad restaurant?
boxes.why: Mistakes on the bill are a bad sign.
A cosy place feels nice and relaxing.

boxes.q: Which part comes at the end of an essay?
What gives the main idea of a paragraph?
boxes.why: The topic sentence states the main idea.

boxes.q: Which title suits an essay about a bad meal?

o: the decoration and style of a room
boxes.why: Décor is how a place looks.

boxes.q: What is the 'body' of an essay?
o: The paragraphs between the introduction and conclusion
boxes.why: The body tells the main events.

boxes.q: Why should events be in order?
o: So the essay flows and is easy to read
boxes.why: A clear order helps the reader.

hunt.q: The style and decoration of a room
Gives the main idea of a paragraph
The final paragraph of an essay
A sign of a bad restaurant

o: Usually the first sentence of a paragraph that gives the main idea
The last sentence of the essay
mcq.why: It tells the reader what the paragraph is about.

mcq.q: What should a narrative essay have at the beginning?
o: An introduction that gives background and catches the reader's attention
mcq.why: A good start sets the scene.

mcq.q: Which list contains only phrases for a good restaurant?
o: delicious food, varied menu, reasonable prices, attentive service
rude waiters, dirty cutlery, large cockroaches, errors on the bill
delicious food, rude waiters, varied menu, dirty cutlery
errors on the bill, reasonable prices, large cockroaches, varied menu

mcq.q: What do you do before writing your first draft?
o: Make notes and share ideas with a group

mcq.q: Topic sentence: 'The service was terrible.' Which is the best supporting detail?
o: The waiter was rude and forgot our order.
The restaurant has a varied menu.
mcq.why: A supporting detail gives an example of the main idea.

mcq.q: Which is a good ending for 'A Nightmare Meal'?
o: We never went back, and from that day we always read reviews first.
I have always loved eating out.
First, we arrived at the restaurant.

mcq.q: Choose the linking word: 'First, we found a table. ___, we ordered our food.'
Why is 'I have always loved eating out, but one meal was special.' a good opening?
o: It gives background and makes the reader want to know more
It is a supporting detail about prices
It is a list of dishes

mcq.q: A restaurant has cosy décor but errors on the bill. What is the best description?
o: It has good and bad points
mcq.why: Cosy décor is good; bill errors are bad.

mcq.q: Why should you write the story ending with your own ideas?
o: To practise creating your own writing instead of copying
Because the text has no story
mcq.why: Your own ideas show your writing skills.
